column1: # The four games that produced the 10 `Incomplete mating PV` lines the
# candidate emitted in S147's clean 3000-game run. Root FEN and the moves
# played up to the last search that warned, taken verbatim from the
# `Position;` and `Moves;` lines fastchess printed beside each warning.
# Kept because the log is gitignored and this is the reproduction.
# `E_mate_minus9` is the one search S170's own --fast run still warned on, added
# 2026-09-02 with `guard` `no` on the reading that its `mate -9` was a distance
# the position does not hold. S171 measured that reading and it is wrong: an
# 18-ply line from that root is legal throughout and ends in checkmate, and the
# engine prints it itself at Hash=256, where the entries the walk needs survive.
# The score is sound and not optimal -- the position is mate in 7 -- and a
# depth-limited search naming a longer mate than the game value is the search
# and not the report. So the row is guarded from S171 on. DEC-127.
# `go` and `start` are the cheapest reproduction found for each case, swept
# 2026-09-02: `start` is the first ply searched, so the plies before it warm
# nothing, and a case that survives a late start costs the gate less. Both are
# fragile by nature -- the defect is a property of what the table happens to
# hold -- which is why the test asserts a mate line was seen at all before
# asserting none of them is short.
# `stride` is how many plies separate the searches, added by S171. A game
# gives one engine only the positions *it* moves from: it never searches the
# ones its opponent moved from, so half the plies write nothing to its table.
# Searching every ply is therefore a table a game does not produce, and
# `F_mate6_inherited_no_line` is the case that showed it -- it reproduces at
# stride 2 and never at stride 1, which is why the first three attempts to
# reproduce it from the census log came back clean. Rows 1 to 5 are stride 1,
# the shape they were found and measured in; nothing about them changes.
# `start` and `stride` must leave the last ply on the schedule, which is what
# the guard checks when it reads the row.
# THE `go` BUDGETS ARE VALID ONLY FOR THE ZOBRIST KEY SET THEY WERE CHOSEN
# UNDER. The class is table eviction and the keys decide which entries evict
# which, so a redraw retires them: over four arbitrary seeds on 2026-09-08 every
# one left three or four of the six cases reporting no mate at all.
# The games survive it and only the budgets move. S203 redrew the keys and
# re-swept all three affected rows back -- A 300000 -> 1000000,
# one rule stated in `adocs/data/S203_case_sweep.sh` and applied to every row:
# the cheapest budget at which the case reports at least its floor of mate lines
# with all of them complete. Run that script after anything that moves the tree,
# not only after a key change; it re-derives these budgets and the floors in
# tests/test_mate_carry.cpp both. DEC-154, DEC-156, DEC-142.
# The grid is a knife edge, which is the thing to expect rather than be
# surprised by: C reports 13 mate lines at 1500000 nodes and 0 at both 1000000
